prompt: ProDevelop orders the equipment it uses to develop film for its customers over the Internet from the FilmCo.com web site. What type of e-commerce business model is represented?
explanation: Business-to-business (B2B). Business-to-business e-commerce occurs when businesses use the Internet to buy and sell goods from each other. A primary example of this is when one business orders its supplies from another. In a business-to-consumer e-commerce model, businesses sell products over the Internet to consumers. This is what most people think of when they think of e-commerce. Consumer-to-consumer e-commerce occurs when consumers (i.e., the end-users) buy and sell goods from each other over the Internet on sites such as eBay.com and other auction sites. At this point, there is really no such thing as consumer-to-business e-commerce; although, the constantly changing nature of the Internet always opens the door to new business models.

prompt: Selling goods and services through the use of catalogs, mail order, vending machines, and sites on the Web are examples of
explanation: Nonstore retailing. Nonstore retailing involves selling in other than actual store locations. There is no store for customers to visit; therefore, the selling takes place through the use of catalogs, mail order, vending machines, sites on the Web, etc. Nonstore retailing offers many of the same goods and services that traditional retailing offers and provides customers with another method of obtaining the products they want and need. Scrambled merchandising involves selling a variety of unrelated items. Target marketing is the identification and selection of markets for a business or for a product. Product franchising is a method of distributing products through a licensing arrangement between the parent company and the franchisee.

prompt: In what marketing activity do online businesses engage in order to meet the wants and needs of consumers?
explanation: Product/Service management. This marketing function involves developing a product mix in response to market opportunities. Online businesses try to determine what products consumers need or want in order to provide those products. Cost-benefit analysis is comparing the expense of an activity to the benefits received from the activity. National advertising is the promotion of products throughout the country. Risk management is the planning, controlling, preventing, and procedures used by management to limit business losses.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a brick and click store placing a blanket order with a vendor:
choices: Ordering goods that are out of stock
Ordering items in advance of the season
Ordering items that usually are not carried
explanation: Ordering goods without specifying style. Relying on vendors to ship an appropriate assortment of goods is an example of placing a blanket order. For example, a brick and click store might order towels and sheets and rely on the vendor to ship an assortment of colors, sizes, and styles. When placing a blanket order, stores also might allow a vendor to decide when to ship and how much to ship at one time. Ordering goods that are out of stock is an example of placing a reorder. Ordering items that usually are not carried is an example of placing a special order. Ordering items in advance of the season is an example of placing an advance order.

prompt: Calculate an e-business's cash receipts for one month based on the following information: sells assets worth $5,100, earns $245 in interest, has cash sales of $3,625, and has credit sales of $1,675.
explanation: $8,970. Cash receipts are the specific sources of money flowing into the e-business from such things as interest income and the sale of goods and assets. Only collected money, not monies owed to the business from credit sales, is recorded under cash receipts. In this example, add the sale of assets, interest, and cash sales to determine cash receipts ($5,100 + $245 + $3,625 = $8,970).

prompt: Susan has a middle management position in her company. Her primary job responsibility is likely to be
choices: developing the plans and goals for the company.
being responsible for other managers or supervisors.
spending one day a week on each management function.
establishing the weekly work schedules for employees.
explanation: Being responsible for other managers or supervisors. Mid-level, or middle, managers report to top-level management and have supervisors who report to them. Plans and goals for the company are developed by top management. Susan is likely to be involved in some aspect(s) of more than one management function at any one time. Establishing weekly work schedules is a task of supervisory, or first-level, managers who work directly with the employees who carry out the business's routine work.

prompt: Who is responsible for developing a quality culture in an Internet business?
explanation: All employees. A quality culture cannot exist in an Internet business unless all employees are involved. Although some employees are more directly involved, everyone must participate. For example, management must provide the guidance and direction as well as the tools necessary for employees to do quality work. The production staff must do their best to produce a quality product, and salespeople must provide quality service to customers. Support personnel, such as accounting clerks and delivery people, also must be committed to doing a quality job. Everyone must do their part and work together to develop a quality culture.

prompt: A primary reason why there are so many new trends in e-commerce is because of the
choices: constantly changing nature of the Internet.
many laws that regulate the Internet.
lack of sales opportunities on the Internet.
explanation: Constantly changing nature of the Internet. The Internet is always changing; technology seems to get more sophisticated every day, and e-tailers consistently find news ways to sell products to customers. The Internet's usefulness is far from being limited because there are so many opportunities for doing business on the Web. There are countless opportunities to sell to a global market 24/7, which actually results in new trends in e-commerce such as web pages in different languages. Trends in e-commerce would actually diminish as more and more restrictive laws prevent entrepreneurship from flourishing on the Internet; businesses would concentrate on selling through traditional methods rather than finding new ways to sell over the Internet.

prompt: What procedure should always be performed before posting a web page on a web server?
choices: Review the page to make sure the content meets international trade requirements
Consult an attorney to verify the accuracy of the web-page legal content
Test the page to identify broken links, missing images, or unclear instructions
Apply for a patent to protect the web-page contents from plagiarism
explanation: Test the page to identify broken links, missing images, or unclear instructions. Broken links and unclear instructions make it difficult, if not impossible, for readers to obtain information or purchase products from a web site. Therefore, it is important to make sure that all elements of the web page work properly. Generally, web pages are not patented. A patent doesn't necessarily protect web-page content from plagiarism. Although it is a good idea to consult an attorney regarding legal content posted on web pages, not all web pages include legal content. Therefore, it is not a procedure that should always be performed. Web-page content is not subject to international trade requirements.

prompt: One way that Internet companies try to protect their customers' credit-card information when they are buying online is by providing
explanation: Secure sites. Internet companies that sell their goods and services online provide secure sites on which customers can submit credit-card information. These sites are designed in such a way that it is extremely difficult for unauthorized users to access them. Although Internet companies offer secure sites and take other measures to protect customers' transactions, the possibility still exists that sophisticated hackers will find ways to circumvent the system. Privacy statements explain a company's policy concerning customers' privacy. Internet companies usually do not provide insurance coverage to customers. Internet companies usually provide free access to their sites in order to attract customers and generate sales.

prompt: Freedom from danger, risk, or injury in the workplace is known as
explanation: Employee safety. Both employers and employees can promote safety in the workplace. Employer liability is the employer's responsibility for some action or condition in the workplace. Occupational choice is an individual's choice of career. Someone with job security does not fear loss of the job.

prompt: One disadvantage to the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act of 2000 is that
choices: a computer hacker could intercept the signature and use it illegally.
individuals using electronic signatures are charged a service fee.
electronic signatures are not considered legal in confirming contracts.
it requires electronic signatures to gain governmental approval before each use.
explanation: A computer hacker could intercept the signature and use it illegally. Even with privacy protection in place, it is possible for someone to breech security and use electronic signatures without the owner's permission. Credit-card applications, loans, and many other business arrangements are now done on the Internet, and there are no standards to verify the signature. The Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act does not specify that service fees are charged for using electronic signatures. Electronic signatures are considered legal as a method to finalize a contractual agreement. Governmental approval is not required before each use of electronic signatures.

prompt: Which of the following is one of the responsibilities of the Fair Labor Standards Act:
explanation: Regulates child labor. The Fair Labor Standards Act contains provisions that regulate child labor. It includes strict controls on businesses that hire children under the age of 16, such as the number of hours they are allowed to work and the times they are allowed to work. The act also prohibits businesses from hiring minors between the ages of 16 and 18 to work in hazardous occupations. The Fair Labor Standards Act does not prohibit discrimination, provide worker compensation, or require equal pay.

prompt: When Christy, a sales manager at a large web-site design firm, wants to talk with several members of the sales staff on the telephone at the same time, she could use a service called
explanation: Conference calling. Conference calling can include a number of persons at different locations and is frequently used for business discussions. Call waiting lets the telephone user know someone else is trying to get a call through to that number. The call forwarding feature allows for incoming calls to be transferred to other phone lines. Speed calling allows the caller to dial frequently used telephone numbers with a code that consists of just one or two numbers.

prompt: A simple, or short, report differs from a complex report in that the simple report is
explanation: Less formal. A simple, or short, report is less formal than a long, or complex, report. It is often presented in a memo form so that the recipients can read it quickly and use the information in their decision making. A simple report is less comprehensive than a complex report.

prompt: The title page of a complex written report includes information about the subject matter and the authors and is part of the __________ of the report.
explanation: Front matter. The title page is part of the front matter or preliminaries of a complex written report that is designed to prepare readers for the information that will follow. The table of contents is also part of the front matter. The introduction is part of the body of the complex report, and the appendix is part of the end matter.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason for conducting regular staff meetings:
choices: To give employees time to relax from work
To allow employees to ask questions
explanation: To allow employees to ask questions. Presenting important information at a meeting gives employees the opportunity to ask questions about any points that are not clear. This is an advantage of oral rather than written communication. Disciplinary problems are personal and should be handled privately. New employees need to be oriented at the time they begin work, and staff meeting time should not be used for this purpose or to give employees a work break.

prompt: Which of the following is a purpose of packaging:
choices: To categorize merchandise by type, stock number, or other identifying characteristics
To count and check goods as they are received
To gather together goods requested from within the company or by outside customers
To protect products until they reach consumers
explanation: To protect products until they reach consumers. Before most goods can be handled or moved, they must be packaged in some way. Packaging activities include wrapping, bottling or boxing, color-coding, price-marking, placing in appropriate containers, adding cushioning materials, and attaching shipping tags. Counting and checking goods as they are received are examples of receiving responsibilities. Categorizing merchandise by type, stock number, or other identifying characteristics defines sorting. Gathering together goods requested from within the company or by outside customers defines assembling shipments.

prompt: When products go from the producer to an intermediary before going on to consumers, a(n) __________ channel of distribution is being used.
explanation: Indirect. In an indirect channel, products pass through the hands of such intermediaries as sales agents, wholesalers, and retailers. When a direct channel of distribution is used, products move directly from the producer to the consumer. Direct routes are shorter than indirect routes. Vertical channels refer to distribution systems that are centrally controlled.

prompt: Which of the following is a type of agreement between a buyer and a seller that the Clayton Act makes illegal:
explanation: Tying contract. A tying contract, or agreement, is an illegal agreement requiring a customer to buy other products in order to obtain desired goods and services. The Clayton Act, a federal regulation intended to prevent specific business actions that might prohibit competition, makes tying agreements illegal. Credit arrangements, joint ventures, and territory assignments are not regulated by the Clayton Act.

prompt: Based on the premise that it is less expensive to maintain an existing account than to develop a new one, what must supply-chain managers consider in all phases of the distribution process?
explanation: Customer satisfaction. Customer service and satisfaction directly impacts the bottom line in any business. Successfully meeting the customers' needs and wants can determine a business's success or failure. Channel capabilities, transportation methods, and price competition impact the cost of doing business and should be adjusted to meet the needs of the customer, thus increasing customer satisfaction.

prompt: When a customer places an order at quickdelivery.com, the order immediately travels over the Internet to a distribution center that ships out the merchandise within 24 hours. This is an example of
explanation: Electronic customer relationship management (e-CRM). Electronic customer relationship management makes use of technology to develop positive associations with customers. An example would be sending a customer's order over the Internet to the distribution center right away so that it can be delivered in a speedy manner. Mail relaying refers to the process of using another business's mail server to hide the identity of the sender of e-mail messages. Authentication refers to the process of granting or denying access to information such as after a customer enters a password or uses a credit card to place an order. Secure sockets layer (SSL) is a security measure that protects online credit-card transactions using encryption and a mechanism by which only the merchant's software is able to unscramble the data.

prompt: One way businesses benefit by using a computerized information system in logistics management is that it
choices: eliminates the human error that is created in a manual system.
reduces the need to implement satellite-tracking programs.
provides immediate access to data used in tracking the order process.
generates a higher profit margin on slow-moving inventory.
explanation: Provides immediate access to data used in tracking the order process. Information technology has made it easier for businesses to get a complete view of company operations. Computer systems allow businesspeople to track the order from order placement through the delivery process. Use of technical information systems does not necessarily generate a higher profit margin on slow-moving material. The longer a product is stored, the more it is costing the company. Computerized information systems do not necessarily reduce the need for satellite-tracking programs or eliminate human error. Since humans operate computers, there is always a chance of data entry error.

prompt: One way to reduce online customers' frustration and keep the customers informed of the status of their orders is through
explanation: Out-of-stock notifications. Notifying the customer that a certain item is out of stock is part of the order fulfillment process. Keeping the customer informed allows the customer to make another selection. Digital delivery is the delivery of products through electronic means. Virtual stores do not house stock, but provide for direct delivery from suppliers. Shopping carts allow for online customer shopping, but do not notify of out-of-stock items.

prompt: When an e-tailer receives goods shipped FOB factory that were damaged in transit, the e-tailer should file a claim with the
explanation: Carrier. The carrier, or shipping company, is responsible for the goods while in transit. The vendor, or consignor, is the shipper and is not responsible for the safety of a shipment shipped FOB factory. These terms mean that the buyer owns the goods from the time they leave the seller, and the buyer must file any claims for damages in transit directly with the carrier. The receiving department records all damaged goods and usually files the claim.

prompt: What are the primary factors that e-tailers consider when determining the most appropriate shipping method for merchandise?
explanation: Delivery time and carton weight. Many factors must be considered when determining appropriate shipping methods. Many transportation services set delivery charges based on the weight of the merchandise. Other major considerations include the time it takes to transport the merchandise depending on the type of transportation (e.g., air, ground, rail, water), and the distance between the sender and the recipient. For example, a 50-pound carton shipping via air freight that travels a distance of 2,000 miles to arrive the next day generally costs more than a 50-pound carton shipping via truck that travels a distance of 1,000 miles in three days. Although insurance can be purchased to cover loss during transportation, it is generally a primary consideration only if the item is very expensive. A credit rating refers to a system that evaluates an individual's or business's ability to pay debt (e.g., mortgage) on a timely basis. The transportation company might want to verify the e-tailer's credit rating before making contractual agreements. Therefore, the credit rating is not necessarily a primary consideration for the e-tailer but for the shipping company. Although some locations might charge sales tax on shipping, many places do not. Therefore, sales tax is not a primary consideration.

prompt: Jacque's Online Art Supplies orders goods whenever an employee notices that a certain product's quantity is low. What type of periodic unit control inventory system is the business using?
explanation: Visual control. When using visual control, employees simply look over the stock from time to time to see what is in short supply. A physical count determines the precise amount of stock on hand at the time of the count by tallying each unit of stock. Tickler control is a rotating system of counting portions of stock at regular intervals, rather than counting all of the stock at once. Concentric control is a distractor.

prompt: An architectural firm electronically transfers drawings over the Internet to a blueprint company that prints, packages, and sends the drawings to clients. This addition of a channel member to facilitate business is an example of
explanation: Reintermediation. When businesses add channel members to make distribution more efficient, it is referred to as reintermediation. An example would be sending drawings to a blueprint company over the Internet so that the drawings can be printed, packaged, and sent to clients rather than doing these tasks in-house. Disintermediation is just the opposite of intermediation because it eliminates middlemen that normally help in the transfer of products from the producer to the ultimate consumer. Hosting refers to storing web pages on a server for a monthly fee. Unit control is a way of keeping track of inventory according to the number of physical units of stock.

prompt: When selecting a channel of distribution, an online business must consider where its customers are located. This consideration is part of which of the following categories of factors affecting channel selection:
explanation: Market. Market factors deal with where the consumers are, who they are, the information they require, and the size of their orders. Product factors deal with the nature of the product. Producer factors deal with the amount of the producer's funds, the size of the sales force, and the amount of control desired over the channel. Factors related to intermediaries include whether to use them and whether their services are worth the cost.

prompt: E-businesses regularly meet with channel members to discuss problems and improve performance in order to develop
explanation: Long-term partnerships. Most e-businesses want to develop long-term partnerships with channel members because it is more cost effective to maintain a relationship with an existing member than to locate new channel members. To accomplish this, businesses often meet regularly with channel members to discuss problems and evaluate performance. This gives both the business and the channel members an opportunity to discuss problems and decide on a mutually satisfactory solution. By working together, the business and the channel members can improve performance and develop a long-term partnership. Businesses and channel members do not meet regularly to develop transportation systems, cost-effective inventories, or routine buying procedures.

prompt: Under which of the following circumstances might producers be willing to pay higher prices for natural resources:
explanation: Supplies are limited. Many natural resources are limited because they are difficult to obtain, because the supply is running out, or because they are affected by weather conditions. When natural resources are limited, producers often are willing to pay more in order to obtain the resource. They need the resource to produce goods and will pay more in order to continue production. Producers usually are not willing to pay higher prices for natural resources because the owners are persuasive or alternatives are available. Producers might be willing to pay more for human resources if workers are skilled.

prompt: Which of the following types of economic systems is used in the United States:
explanation: Market. The United States has a market economy in which the means of production and distribution are owned and controlled by individuals and businesses. In a traditional economy, people produce only what they must have in order to exist. A command economy is one in which all or many of the means of production and distribution are owned and controlled by the government. In a socialist, or modified command, economy, government owns the basic means of production, but there is private ownership of businesses as well.

prompt: If an online business receives an insurance payment because of a loss by fire, this would be the result of a(n) __________ risk.
explanation: Pure. Pure risks are risks that carry with them the possibility of loss or no loss. Pure risks are generally insurable. Speculative risks are risks that may result in a loss, no change, or a gain. Economic risks are changes in the market that force prices to be lowered. Human risks are caused by human weakness and unpredictability.

prompt: A situation in which there is only one supplier of a certain good or service is called
explanation: Monopoly. Monopolies typically exist when the market is controlled by one supplier, and there are no substitute products readily available. An oligopoly exists when a few large producers offer essentially the same product, e.g., automobiles. Competition is the rivalry between similar businesses.

prompt: Jamie is a new employee who does not want to join a union, but he was told he will have to join after his probationary period because his company is a(n) __________ shop.
explanation: Union. Union shops require all employees to join the union after their probationary period. Closed shops are illegal in all states because they require individuals to be members of a union before they can be hired. Open shops do not require employees to join a union or pay dues. Agency shops require nonunion members to pay dues.

prompt: Which of the following economic problems may cause an increase in the level of unemployment:
explanation: High interest rates. High interest rates are an economic problem that may lead to an increase in unemployment because businesses often do not want to borrow money to expand when interest rates are high. When businesses do not expand, there is a shortage of jobs for new workers entering the labor force which often leads to an increase in the level of unemployment. Federal income taxes and social welfare costs are not considered economic problems. A trade deficit is an unfavorable balance of trade in which a nation's imports are greater than its exports.

prompt: The advantage of e-commerce to small online marketers is that it gives them access to
explanation: International customers. Online marketing allows businesses to make their goods and services available to customers throughout the world. By creating a page on the Internet, even small businesses make it possible for people in other countries to see their products and place orders. The impact on international trade is significant because businesses that previously sold only to local customers can now sell to anyone who has access to a computer. E-commerce involves selling online rather than providing access to local manufacturers, specialized vendors, or potential investors.

prompt: XYZ Company is interested in developing, producing, and selling a new web-site design product. Before it does so, the company spends six months conducting marketing research. What are the primary advantages of this course of action?
choices: To delay the production process and increase labor costs
To increase costs and determine consumer dislikes
To predict trends and provide information to customers
To determine customer preferences and minimize losses
explanation: To determine customer preferences and minimize losses. Businesses obtain marketing information in order to develop a web-site design product that customers want and need. By doing research, companies obtain marketing information that helps them to minimize the losses that may occur from introducing a product that customers do not want. Businesses do not conduct marketing research to increase costs, although they may identify consumer dislikes. The goal is not to delay production or increase labor costs. Marketing research may identify trends, but it is not intended to provide information to customers.

prompt: Secondary sources such as census reports, other government publications, trade magazines, or chambers of commerce are excellent sources for obtaining information about
explanation: Demographics. Demographic information provides data about consumer characteristics such as age, sex, occupation, income, education, health, and marital status. This information is usually available from secondary sources, which can be accessed easily and at no cost. These sources do not provide information about competing products or business personnel. Businesses often use demographic information to identify characteristics of the target market.

prompt: Which of the following is an important factor that Internet businesses should consider when developing a marketing-information management system:
choices: Type of system used by competitors
Who has access to the system
explanation: Who has access to the system. When developing a marketing-information management system, an Internet business should consider who will have access to the information in the system. Some businesses accumulate confidential information that they do not want to be accessible to all employees. These businesses might restrict access to specific employees who compile the information or to managers who use the information. Other businesses gather information that is not confidential or secret and is accessible to all employees. Where the system is located, the hours the system will operate, and the type of system used by competitors are not important factors that a business considers when developing a marketing-information management system.

prompt: Which of the following is a major privacy issue in e-commerce that concerns businesses and their customers:
explanation: Retail transactions. Privacy is a major concern in e-commerce because of the type of personal information that is required to make purchases. Customers need to provide credit card numbers as well as addresses and other personal information in order to complete retail transactions. What businesses do with this information and whether they share it with others is of concern to customers. Customers are also concerned with the safety of their financial information. Many businesses develop privacy policies that they post on their web sites to assure customers that their personal information will be protected. Membership fees, intellectual property, and site management are not major privacy issues.

prompt: Why do many Internet companies maintain and update their customer database on a regular basis?
choices: So their promotional budgets can be increased
So Internet service provider fees can be reduced
explanation: To reduce wasted marketing efforts. Many Internet surfers access web sites that display goods or services that do not fit their needs. Sometimes, web users sign up for a product or service and do not need it after a period of time. Without strategies in place to maintain a business's database, the information system can grow out of control. As a result, promotional information, e-mail marketing messages, and newsletters are often sent to people who are not going to purchase goods or services. This is a waste of time in terms of money and personnel. Therefore, many companies try to update their databases regularly so information is sent to those who are potential or existing customers. One means of maintaining a database is providing web users an opt-out link to discontinue receiving unwanted information from the company. Maintaining a database does not necessarily lead a company to increase its promotional budget nor does it accelerate a web-site's download time. Internet service providers are companies that provide access to the Internet. Fees are not necessarily reduced when companies update their databases.

prompt: What is a web-site tracking method that many e-tailers use to help them make decisions about which products to feature?
explanation: Cookies. A cookie is a programming code that allows web sites to track visitor behavior. E-tailers use cookies to obtain information about visitors to their web sites such as how often they visit the site and what they buy. Cookies allow e-tailers to get to know their customers' habits and preferences. Then, e-tailers use the information to decide which products to feature and what type of content to offer that will appeal to their customers. Spiders and crawlers are programs that identify and review web sites. A browser is software that allows a computer to access information on the Internet.

prompt: What is the range of times people accessed a business's web site if 20 people accessed the site 8 times a month, 45 people accessed the site 7 times a month, 72 people accessed the site 6 times a month, 58 people accessed the site 5 times a month, and 32 people accesssed the site 4 times a month?
explanation: 4. Range is the distance between the highest value and the lowest value. In this example, 8 is the highest value because it represents the most times during the month that the people responding accessed the business's web site.The lowest number of times the people responding accessed the web site was 4 times a month. To calculate the range, subtract the lowest value from the highest value (8 - 4 = 4).

prompt: If an online business decides to make product changes, it must also make changes in all the other elements of the
explanation: Marketing mix. The marketing mix is the combination of the four elements of marketing—product, place, promotion, and price. The elements of the marketing mix are interrelated, and they depend on each other. A change in one element, therefore, will need to be coordinated with a change in the other elements. A master plan is an organized list of all the activities an individual plans to accomplish in a given amount of time on a specific day. A strategic goal is a long-range objective. A sales policy is a general rule established by management to guide the personal selling effort and outline sales procedures.

prompt: Which demographic segmentation characteristic should an e-tailer consider when promoting expensive, fine jewelry to consumers?
explanation: Income. Income level should be the first characteristic considered because e-tailers must promote their products to markets that have the ability to purchase. In this case, that market is possibly people with high incomes. Customers of all ages, either gender, and any life stage may desire jewelry but may be limited in purchasing by their income level.

prompt: Which of the following do Internet businesses use to identify developing changes so that they can make adjustments to remain competitive:
explanation: Environmental scanning. Internet businesses need to understand changes in their environment in order to adapt and remain competitive. They often use a procedure known as environmental scanning to gather information about changes or trends that are beginning to develop in the marketplace. This procedure allows businesses to identify changes at an early stage and decide if they present a threat to the way the business is currently operating. Businesses do not use geographic monitoring, demographic segmenting, or psychological profiling to identify changes that are developing.

prompt: A SWOT analysis indicates that customers' buying preferences are changing, but the online business has a very limited product line. This is an example of an
choices: internal strength responding to an external threat.
external threat attacking an internal weakness.
internal weakness compensating for an external threat.
external opportunity coinciding with an internal strength.
explanation: External threat attacking an internal weakness. External threats often create problems for an online business's internal weaknesses. For example, a SWOT analysis indicates that customers' buying preferences are changing, however, the business has a very limited product line. The external threat is that customers want a different type of product; but the business only offers a limited number of products, which is a weakness. The problem for the business is that customers will buy from other companies that offer more variety. Unless the business can adjust and overcome its weakness, it will probably lose sales. The SWOT analysis did not indicate an internal strength responding to an external threat, an internal weakness compensating for an external threat, or an external opportunity coinciding with an internal strength.

prompt: Under which of the following circumstances might it be useful for an e-business to develop a long-term sales forecast:
explanation: Unchanging market. A sales forecast can be prepared for any length of time that is useful to the e-business. One factor that affects how far ahead a business can predict its sales is conditions in the market. For example, if there has been a steady demand for the company's products and the market is not expected to change, a long-term forecast might be appropriate. Short-term sales forecasts usually are prepared if a business has insufficient operating capital or the economy is unstable. Intermediate forecasts often work well for businesses that are planning to expand.

prompt: What approach to sales forecasting is being used by an Internet business that starts the process by making forecasts for individual products or product lines?
explanation: Bottom-up. The bottom-up, or build-up, approach involves starting the sales forecast process by gathering individual forecasts which may be combined, or built up, into a forecast for the entire Internet company. This approach is the opposite of the top-down approach which involves starting the sales forecasting process by preparing an overall forecast for the entire company. A trading area is the territory in which a firm conducts business. A sales quota is a specific selling goal set for a member of the sales force.

prompt: An important step in the process of developing a marketing plan involves selecting the
explanation: Target market. The target market is the group of consumers on whom the business focuses its marketing efforts. An important part of developing a marketing plan involves selecting the target market because the purpose of the marketing plan is to establish procedures or strategies for attracting those target customers. A business needs to know which customers it is trying to reach in order to make decisions about how to reach them. Businesses often conduct research in order to gather important information before starting to develop a marketing plan. Once a marketing plan has been developed, a business might select a distribution agent and a sales force.

prompt: What do many online businesses analyze to determine if their marketing efforts are effectively reaching their target market?
explanation: Customer satisfaction. One of the best ways for an online business to determine if its marketing efforts are effectively reaching the target market is to analyze customer satisfaction. To do this, a business often keeps track of the number of new customers it attracts, the number of customers it loses, and the number of customers who have complained. It also monitors customers' awareness of the business and its products as well as what customers think about quality and service. Businesses then use this information to measure the level of customer satisfaction. If businesses identify problem areas, they can make adjustments in their marketing efforts to correct the situation. Exclusive distribution involves making goods available only in certain locations. The procurement process is the process of purchasing goods and services. Vertical integration occurs when a business is involved in many aspects of the industry.

prompt: Besides having a clear understanding of what you want from negotiation, it is important to also know
choices: how long negotiation is expected to take.
how many people you will be negotiating with.
who will be required to implement the outcome of the negotiation.
explanation: What the other person wants. Knowing what the other person wants allows you to identify the common ground between the two viewpoints. How long negotiation will take is seldom determined ahead of time. Although it may be nice to know, the number of people attending is not a crucial factor in negotiations. The task at hand is the negotiation. It is unwise to divide your focus between the negotiation and implementing the outcome.

prompt: One way that employees can control and manage their level of stress is to
choices: add more responsibility to their lives.
explanation: Set realistic standards for themselves. Employees who set realistic standards for themselves rather than expecting perfection all the time are usually able to control and manage their level of stress. It is important for employees to understand that they cannot perform perfectly in all situations and that they will make some mistakes. Being aware of this helps employees to manage stress because they will not set their goals so high that they will often be unable to achieve them. Striving to obtain perfection all the time increases stress and may cause employees to think that they are failures if they don't live up to those expectations. Adding more responsibility often increases stress. Hurrying to complete complicated tasks is an indication that employees are experiencing stress. Developing friendships is an effective way to reduce stress.

prompt: What is an important activity that Internet businesses should include in project planning in order to improve the chances of the project being successful?
explanation: Communication. Communication is an exchange of information, which is an important part of project planning. In order for a project to succeed, everyone involved in developing and carrying out the project needs to know the goals, strategies, and expected outcomes of the project. Sufficient information needs to be communicated during all phases of planning in order for those involved to be able to provide input and to perform their assigned tasks. Orientation is job preparation or induction training for new employees. Compensation is wages, incentives, and benefits offered an employee. Negotiation involves compromise in order to resolve a problem or dispute.

prompt: Before developing a project plan for an Internet company, the manager must identify the
explanation: Objectives. A project is a new or one-time activity that is executed through a series of interdependent tasks and resources and is completed within a specific time frame. Before an e-commerce manager can begin planning how to execute a project, the objectives, or goals, must be identified. After objectives are established, the manager must determine the cost, time lines, schedules, benefits, resources, and necessary tasks to complete the endeavor.

prompt: Which of the following should guide a supervisor who is handling an employee's complaint:
explanation: Background facts. Many factors often enter into an employee complaint. A supervisor should focus on learning as much as possible about the real problem behind the complaint in order to handle it correctly. A supervisor should strive to be as objective as possible in identifying the actual problem. To do this, the supervisor should keep his/her inhibitions, personal feelings, and cultural or socioeconomic biases to a minimum.

prompt: It is the responsibility of a supervisor to give an assessment to management of what an employee does well on the job as well as what needs to be improved. This report to management is called a(n)
explanation: Employee evaluation. Through evaluation, managers are able to inform employees of their strengths and weaknesses. Once these are identified, management can take steps to help employees increase their strengths and minimize their weaknesses. A reference provides information about a job applicant that will help to determine if the applicant should be hired. A job specification includes information as to the nature of the work done in a particular job, the necessary qualifications needed by the employee to do the work, and the opportunities the job offers. An employee requisition is a request sent to the personnel department for a new worker.

prompt: Telephone charges are an example of which of the following types of operating expenses:
explanation: Semivariable. Semivariable expenses are business costs that vary to some extent in response to sales. These expenses do not fall neatly into the pattern of fixed or variable costs. Telephone expense is considered a semivariable cost because it includes a fixed monthly service charge as well as toll charges that vary with usage and sales levels. Predictable and reliable expenses are those costs that remain fairly constant. Flexible expenses change according to changes in sales volume.

prompt: An important reason why most click and brick businesses carry out regular maintenance activities is to
explanation: Protect their investment. A click and brick business usually has a considerable amount of money tied up in whatever kind of equipment is needed to operate the business. The business can protect this investment by maintaining the equipment so that it will last as long as possible. Misuse of equipment can be prevented by instructing employees in proper handling of the equipment. Construction codes are laws that apply to building a structure. Not all businesses need to pass health inspections.

prompt: Calculate the amount an online business can budget to spend on new warehouse equipment if it estimates sales of $690,000, expenses of $325,000, and designates 25% of profit for equipment purchases.
explanation: $91,250. When online businesses develop budgets, they usually prepare a capital budget that allows a certain amount of money for the purchase of new or replacement equipment. In many cases, the amount they budget is based on a percentage of profit. In this example, to calculate the amount a business can budget for new equipment, first determine the amount of profit by subtracting expenses from sales ($690,000 - $325,000 = $365,000). Then, calculate 25% of profit ($365,000 x 25% or .25 = $91,250).

prompt: An online bookstore's full-time warehouse employee resigned and the bookstore decided to hire two part-time employees to each work four hours a day, five days a week. Calculate the savings to the bookstore for a four-week period if the full-time employee earned $650 a week and the part-time employees will be paid $12.50 an hour.
explanation: $600. Many online bookstores control expenses by hiring part-time employees at an hourly rate rather than salaried full-time employees. The advantage to the bookstore is the same number of employees working during a given time period but for less wages. To calculate the savings in this situation, first determine the payroll expense for the full-time employee by multiplying the weekly salary by four weeks ($650 x 4 = $2,600). Then, determine the payroll expense for one part-time employee by multiplying the number of hours worked each day by five days to find the number of hours worked each week (4 x 5 = 20). Then, multiply that number by the hourly rate to determine the weekly pay ($12.50 x 20 = $250). Multiply the weekly pay by four weeks ($250 x 4 = $1,000) and the four-week total by the two part-time employees ($1,000 x 2 = $2,000). Determine the savings by subtracting the part-time payroll from the full-time payroll ($2,600 - $2,000 = $600).

prompt: A substantial cost associated with e-commerce often is the commission paid to
explanation: Referring web sites. Businesses often arrange with other businesses to place links on each other's web sites so viewers can easily jump from one site to another. When sales result, the business pays a commission to the referring web site. For example, Business A has a link on the web site of Business B, and a customer clicks on the link and is transported to the web site of Business A. The customer makes a purchase and Business A pays Business B a commission for the referral. This is a cost associated with e-commerce that businesses need to consider. A business might decide that the cost of paying commissions is too high based on the level of sales. Because of the nature of e-commerce, businesses usually do not pay commissions to sales associates. Distribution companies are paid fees for shipping and handling rather than commissions. Leasing agents are paid by the property owners rather than by e-commerce business owners.

prompt: Individuals who regularly analyze the results of their decisions often are able to
explanation: Learn from their mistakes. The final step in the decision-making process is evaluating the outcome of the decision. By analyzing the results of their decisions, people often are able to learn from their mistakes and make better decisions in the future. If the outcome of one decision was unfavorable, a person probably would decide not to make the same mistake in the future. Recognizing problems, identifying consequences, and choosing alternatives are earlier steps in the decision-making process.

prompt: Individuals often succeed in occupations that require the skills that match their
explanation: Aptitudes. Aptitudes are natural talents for learning specific skills. Individuals often succeed in occupations that require the skills that match their natural talents. For example, some people have an aptitude for working with numbers while others have an aptitude for working with their hands. People who have an aptitude for working with numbers might be successful in jobs that require those skills such as accounting or bookkeeping. Values are the principles by which people live. Behavior is the manner in which people act. Attitudes are the ways a person looks at life.

prompt: Advertising Age, Hardware Age, and Chain Store Age are examples of
explanation: Trade journals. A trade journal is a publication designed for workers in a particular industry or business. Professional journals are publications designed to inform doctors, lawyers, and other professionals about developments in their professions. Consumer magazines are intended for people with a variety of interests. Class magazines are designed to appeal to a select group of people such as those interested in cars or sports.

prompt: What do online businesses expect to make when they set prices on goods and services?
explanation: Profits. Profit is the monetary reward a business owner receives for taking the risk involved in investing in a business. Online businesses set prices on goods and services that will make a profit. Businesses expect that the sale of goods and services will generate sufficient profit to achieve the return on investment they want. If businesses can't set prices high enough to make a profit, they probably won't market those goods and services. Businesses do not expect to make salaries or payments when they set prices on goods and services. Quotas are specific goals to be met.

prompt: True or False: E-tailers are not required to adhere to the same ethical standards associated with the pricing strategies of price differentials, gouging, and dumping as other companies.
choices: False, if they do not, they will suffer the same consequences that all companies suffer.
True, e-tailers do not market to the same consumers as other companies.
True, the speed of transactions using Internet technology inhibits proving any wrongdoing.
False, e-tailers must adhere to price differential ethical standards but not those related to dumping and gouging.
explanation: False, if they do not, they will suffer the same consequences that all companies suffer. Companies who do not adhere to some type of ethical standard or code of ethics will suffer damaged reputation, long-term loss of trust, and loss of business. E-tailers are expected to adhere to the same ethical standards as other companies. They often market to the same consumers as other companies. Internet technology does not inhibit proving any wrongdoing.

prompt: Who is guilty of unlawful price differential under the Robinson-Patman Act when a buyer for a large e-tailer demands and receives discriminatory prices from a manufacturer?
explanation: Buyer and seller. The Robinson-Patman Act is intended to restrain buyers for large e-tailers from demanding and receiving discriminatory prices. If the seller agrees to the discriminatory prices demanded by the buyer, both are guilty. The seller has a responsibility to not give in to illegal price demands.

prompt: The amount that an e-business charges for a good or a service is known as
explanation: Selling price. Selling price is usually thought of as the dollar figure shown on the price tag of products. Cash flow is the movement of funds into and out of an e-business. Cost of goods is the cost to the business of obtaining products for resale. Profit is the funds a business has left from its sales income after paying its costs and expenses.

prompt: Which of the following would cause an e-tailer to charge higher prices for its products:
choices: Paying a commission for referrals from other sites
Obtaining a cost savings from doing business online
Attracting customers who use the Internet to comparison shop
explanation: Paying a commission for referrals from other sites. When an e-tailer has to pay a commission for sales that result from referrals from other web sites, it usually passes on the cost to customers in the form of higher prices. Engaging in global competition would have the opposite effect (i.e., lower prices) because competition actually drives down prices as businesses try to take customers away from each other. A cost savings from doing business online (e.g., cheaper catalog costs) would result in lower prices because the e-tailer could pass the savings along to customers in the form of cheaper prices. When customers use the Internet to comparison shop, e-tailers offer lower prices in order to remain competitive.

prompt: When products are graded by nongovernmental agencies, the grading is
explanation: Voluntary. The grading of various products is performed on a voluntary basis. Grading is not required by law. Although grading is voluntary, it has become an accepted practice throughout the country because many purchasers prefer to buy products that meet specific quality standards. Occasional and periodic mean infrequently. Mandatory means required.

prompt: What might decrease if an Internet business adds an inappropriate item to the product mix?
explanation: Profits. An Internet business might experience a decrease in profits if it adds an inappropriate item to the product mix. An inappropriate item might compete with the original goods, which would cause sales of the original goods to decline and sales for the new item to be less than expected. Businesses should make sure that their product mix is appropriate in order to increase sales and profits. Expenses are the monies that a business spends. Prices are the amounts of money paid for a good, service, or resource. Salaries are money payments for labor.

prompt: Online businesses that sell services rather than goods often provide which of the following extra services to customers:
explanation: Credit. Many online businesses that sell services offer their customers extended credit or payment plans. Credit is an extra service that businesses offer rather than the service that the businesses sell. For example, a publisher that sells access to online magazines and newspapers may allow customers to pay for those services over a period of time, such as monthly. Services are intangible which means that they cannot be stored, repaired, or shipped.

prompt: An online office supply store that sells ink pens claims that no other pen on the market uses a type of ink that changes color when exposed to light. The store is positioning its product according to what strategy?
choices: Relation to other products in a line
explanation: Unique characteristics. The online office supply store is positioning its product according to unique characteristics because it is claiming that its product does something that no other product can do. The ink changing color in light is a feature, but it is a unique characteristic that is not available on other pens. The store is not positioning according to the quality or price of the pens or their relationship to other products.

prompt: What strategy do many online businesses use in an effort to make customers feel that they are the only ones receiving a special offer?
explanation: Personalization. Personalization involves using an individual's name. Many online businesses try to personalize messages when communicating with customers in order to make the customers feel that they are the only ones receiving a special message or certain information. Personalization helps to build relationships with customers and makes the customers feel that the businesses care enough about them to know their names. Segmentation involves dividing a market into smaller groups. Telemarketing is personal selling that takes place over the telephone. Merchandising is the process of having the right goods in the right place at the right time in order to make a profit.

prompt: The main reason that special online customer services are important in positioning a bank is because they
choices: build goodwill and help increase business.
are part of the principles of bank management.
explanation: Build goodwill and help increase business. Special online customer services help to position a bank. Special online customer services are part of bank-management principles, but are not required by law. Other banks also have them. However, the major factor is the profit that comes from building goodwill and increasing the bank's level of deposits.

prompt: An important customer-service issue in e-commerce involves determining the best method to use to
explanation: Answer customers' questions. Providing service to online customers involves developing a method of answering their questions quickly and accurately. Customers often have questions about products, or the online business's privacy policies, or how to return purchases. Determining the best way to answer these questions is of major concern to online businesses because if customers are not satisfied with the service they receive, they probably will not buy from that business in the future. Advertising is not a customer-service issue. Online businesses usually do not bill customers but expect customers to pay for purchases when ordering. Maintaining inventory levels is a distribution issue.

prompt: Why is it necessary to understand customers when branding?
choices: It enables an e-business to develop a name that accurately reflects the brand.
It helps employees buy into brand values.
It helps the e-business to make lasting emotional and rational connections with customers.
explanation: It helps the e-business to make lasting emotional and rational connections with customers. Successful e-businesses understand everything possible about their customers—their likes, dislikes, habits, and preferences. With this information, businesses can ensure that their operations and touch points, in particular, are customer centric, or built around the customer. This helps build lasting emotional and rational connections between the business's brand and its customers. Understanding customers is not a direct determinant in helping employees buy into brand values, nor is it a direct factor in developing brand names, which are based on brand values and brand promises. Understanding customers does not necessarily lead to making brand decisions that are profitable. In fact, some decisions that are customer focused are not profitable in the short term but lead to long-term relationships.

prompt: If The Deluxe Online Bookstore expects to have $46,750 in sales next month, markdowns equaling 6.5% of sales, and discounts to employees equaling 3% of sales, what is the amount of planned reductions?
explanation: $4,441.25. Planned reductions is the difference between the original price of goods and the final price. Reductions occur because of markdowns, discounts, and shortages. For example, if an online bookstore marks down the price of a book, the store is accepting less for that item than originally planned. Giving employees discounts also reduces the final price. To determine planned reductions, the bookstore first estimates the amount of sales. Then, the store estimates the total percent of reductions, which includes markdowns and discounts (6.5% + 3% = 9.5%). Next, the store multiplies that percentage by the sales estimate to calculate planned reductions ($46,750 x 9.5% or .095 = $4,441.25).

prompt: When is an e-tailer most likely to increase its inventory level?
explanation: Prior to peak selling season. An e-tailer's peak selling season occurs when customer demand for certain products is very high. For example, the demand for beachwear is usually highest during the spring and summer months in the northern hemisphere. Therefore, e-tailers generally try to order these types of items so they have enough on hand to meet demand. If e-tailers order higher quantities of items while in the peak season, they run the risk of stockouts or back orders from their vendors. As a result, e-tailers cannot meet customer demand for seasonal products. Therefore, it is best to order higher amounts of inventory prior to peak season. Most e-tailers do not order higher amounts of stock before conducting physical inventory counts because the process involves more counting and administrative work. Although it is possible that businesses order higher quantities of products after a physical inventory, that it is not always true.

prompt: E-tailers use a merchandising budget to plan stock levels in order to maintain an adequate
explanation: Inventory. The purpose of planning stock levels is to have on hand at all times the amount and variety of merchandise that customers want to buy. Planning stock levels to maintain an adequate inventory is a major benefit of developing a merchandising plan. Planning stock levels is not involved in maintaining an adequate sales staff, public image, or reputation.

prompt: Which of the following is considered to be a disadvantage of promotion:
choices: Promotion can encourage consumers to buy unwanted goods.
Promotion encourages a higher standard of living.
Promotion may enhance a company's image.
explanation: Promotion can encourage consumers to buy unwanted goods. Therefore, some people consider promotion to be manipulative. In many cases, promotion is considered either to be in bad taste, vulgar, or insulting to human intelligence. The fact that promotional activities educate, encourage a higher standard of living, and enhance a company's image are advantages of promotion.

prompt: When an Internet company's promotional activities focus on pointing out differences between its well-established product and competing products, the product is in the __________ stage of its life cycle.
explanation: Maturity. To reach the maturity stage, a product must be well established. Competition increases and focuses on promoting the differences of competing products. During the introductory stage, a product doesn't have much, if any, competition; and the promotional efforts are focused on informing consumers about the product. The growth stage is when competition increases, but the product is not yet well established. Once newer products start taking the place of existing ones, a company's product enters the declining stage and eventually stops production.

prompt: A famous woman was killed in a traffic accident while not wearing a seat belt. Marketers plan to use her image in an online advertising campaign to promote road safety and the use of seat belts. What is one ethical issue that the marketers should consider?
choices: Will it be difficult to find appropriate pictures for the campaign?
Will the public forget the circumstances of the accident?
Will everyone know about the accident?
Will the campaign imply that she was responsible for her own death?
explanation: Will the campaign imply that she was responsible for her own death? Using the image of someone who died in a terrible accident might suggest that the accident was preventable. Marketers need to consider the ethics of using the person's image because the person is not able to give permission. Because of the amount of news coverage given to celebrity events, the public would probably remember, at least through the duration of the campaign. In this type of situation, media pictures are almost always readily available.

prompt: Which of the following statements is true regarding the regulation of Internet promotional activities:
choices: Consumer groups have very little influence with the government regarding advertising legislation.
The regulation of promotional activities applies only to television, radio, and newspaper venues.
Governmental restrictions in regard to promotional activities vary by country.
International laws make it difficult for consumers to sue large companies for unfair advertising practices.
explanation: Governmental restrictions in regard to promotional activities vary by country. Because each government is structured differently, regulation varies from country to country. Consumer advocate groups are organizations that work to influence industry and government policies on behalf of the consumer. Consumer advocate groups often influence government regulation and policies. Because laws vary by country, it would be difficult to develop and fully enforce international laws regarding unfair advertising practices. The ability to sue a company is dependent on the individual country's laws and policies. Many promotional activities are subject to regulation including media venues (television, radio, print); telemarketing; contests; and sweepstakes.

prompt: What part of a print advertisement is often noticed first?
explanation: Illustration. The illustration is a photograph, drawing, painting, or graphic that attracts attention and creates interest. Sometimes, it is the most important part of an advertisement because frequently it is noticed first. The subheadline is in smaller type than the headline and is used to continue the thought expressed in the headline. Body copy is the text of the advertisement. Signature is the name and/or symbol used by the advertiser.

prompt: One of the advantages of using databases in advertising is that it allows online businesses to
explanation: Segment customers. A database is a computerized collection of information. Many online businesses collect a wide variety of information about customers, such as age and location, and maintain this information in a database. Then, businesses can manipulate the data in order to segment customers into specific categories, such as senior citizens, people who live in Florida, or people who earn more than $50,000 a year. Businesses can develop advertising that is directed to the segments that are most likely to buy rather than to all potential customers. The use of databases makes the advertising more effective and less expensive because it targets specific segments of the market. Businesses do not use databases in advertising to identify trends, target suppliers, or analyze forecasts.

prompt: What is one of the main reasons why businesses use e-mail marketing?
explanation: To keep current customers. Using e-mail to follow up with existing customers interests them in buying other products. It can also remind them of when it's time to reorder consumable products such as vitamins and beauty products. Keeping customers is one of the main reasons why businesses use e-mail marketing. A benefit of using e-mail marketing is that businesses can send personal messages to customers. To be most effective, e-mails should be targeted to a specific audience. Also, businesses might duplicate messages.

prompt: Which of the following is often a component of a web site:
explanation: Hyperlink. A hyperlink is a component of an electronic document that can be clicked on to jump to another place within the document or into a different document. Businesses often include hyperlinks on their web sites to allow users to jump to other areas on their site or to related sites. Hyperlink text is underlined, and when users click on it, they are taken to the corresponding web page or web site. A signature is text or images appearing at the bottom of an e-mail indicating a person's or business's identity, contact information, etc. An attachment is a computer file that is sent with an e-mail message. A browser is software that allows a computer to access information on the Internet.

prompt: One way that a business might create interactive public relations is by
choices: reviewing the log files on its web server.
sending out spam mail to potential customers.
establishing a discussion group on its web site.
explanation: Establishing a discussion group on its web site. A business can establish a sense of trust and goodwill by setting up a discussion group on its web site. The group provides a place for members to interact with each other, sharing their ideas, opinions, and resources. Although optimizing with search engines is an important way in which a business can promote its site, it does not provide a way for visitors to interact with the business. Reviewing the log files on the business's web server will provide information about who is visiting the site and what pages are popular; this is a function of marketing-information management, not promotion. Sending out spam mail to potential customers is a public-relations nightmare because it is offensive to most people.

prompt: Which of the following is an external factor that affects the type of promotional plan that an e-business develops:
explanation: Government regulations. An e-business's promotional plan may be affected by regulations imposed by government agencies. Certain government agencies control what businesses are legally able to say about their goods and services. For example, the Federal Trade Commission regulates advertising practices and prohibits unfair and deceptive advertising. This means that businesses may not develop promotional plans that give consumers incorrect or misleading information about their goods or services. Advertising procedures, vendor qualifications, and transportation systems are not factors that affect the type of promotional plan that a business develops.

prompt: An effective way that an Internet business owner might improve the response rate to the business's online advertising program is by
choices: increasing the size of the banner advertisements that appear on major web sites.
creating an online suggestion box so Internet users can provide feedback.
developing customer incentives that correspond with the company's objectives.
using the same version of the advertisement for each site on which the ad appears.
explanation: Developing customer incentives that correspond with the company's objectives. Before response rates can be measured, Internet business owners must establish sales and advertising objectives. To improve response rates, businesses often offer an incentive for those who click on the advertisement. For example, an online publisher might offer a subscription for the online publication free of charge for three months to the Internet users who click on the advertisement. For optimal response rates, the advertisements should be developed to meet the needs of the target audience. A business that has multiple target audiences should use several versions of the advertisement. Although increasing the size of banner advertisements might increase response rates, that does not always happen. If the advertisement is not relevant or is visually unappealing, the Internet user will not click on the advertisement, whether it is large or small. Online suggestion boxes do not necessarily increase response rates to advertisements.

prompt: One of the unique aspects of selling on the Internet is that it is
explanation: Interactive. Selling on the Internet is interactive because it involves two-way electronic communication. Users can interact with the business's web site to locate information, place orders for goods or services, or download data instantly. Frequently, businesses set up their web sites to answer routine questions or to enable customers to e-mail comments directly to the business. The interactive feature of Internet selling allows businesses to respond immediately to customers. For example, a customer buying an airline ticket online can search the site for the best connections and the best price, enter a credit card number for payment, and print a receipt for an e-ticket, all in a matter of minutes. Selling on the Internet is flexible, convenient, and usually effective.

prompt: What can web-site design salespeople do to maintain good relationships with existing customers?
explanation: Live up to their promises. An important part of providing quality customer service involves web-site design salespeople doing what they say they will do. By living up to their promises, salespeople will be able to maintain good relationships with existing customers. Customers will know that they can rely on salespeople and that they will receive the service and support that they need. Breaking promises is a sure way to lose valuable customers. Businesses sometimes use customers in advertisements but that is not a way of maintaining good relationships. Salespeople often ask for referrals from customers with whom they have good relationships, but asking for referrals does not maintain the relationships. It is usually considered inappropriate to send customers expensive gifts that may be misinterpreted as bribes.

prompt: A system that allows a customer-service representative to interactively exchange text-based messages with customers in order to provide direction, answer questions, and trouble-shoot technical glitches is a(n)
explanation: Real-time customer-service chat. This allows representatives to assist customers in real time as they interactively exchange information so the representative can direct the customer to solve the problem. Transactive content is a marketing technique that combines content tailored to a user's profile. Frequently asked questions is a text-based listing of common questions that customers can consult to solve problems. Automated response systems send e-mail order confirmations and acknowledge e-mail inquiries.

prompt: Which of the following will probably happen if a web-site maintenance business does not make an effort to build a clientele:
choices: The business's success will be ensured.
Operating costs will be more easily controlled.
explanation: Customer turnover will be high. A web-site maintenance business that does not make an effort to build a clientele will not retain customers. This increases costs for the business since it is less costly to retain current customers than to seek new ones. Without a group of clients who return regularly, the business will probably fail. Positive word-of-mouth advertising increases when businesses work to build a clientele.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a web-site design salesperson bribing a customer:
choices: Buying lunch during a sales call
Providing tickets to a community activity
Offering half of the commission on a sale
explanation: Offering half of the commission on a sale. Bribery involves giving money or favors to influence a person's decision. An example of a web-site design salesperson bribing a customer is offering to give the customer half of the commission the salesperson receives on a sale. The purpose of the bribe is to persuade the customer to buy from the salesperson. Bribery is usually considered to be unethical because it is not a fair way of doing business. Many companies have guidelines that cover specific situations, such as bribery, to help salespeople behave ethically. While bribery is unethical, giving small and inexpensive gifts is often routine in sales situations. For example, it is acceptable to give an inexpensive gift, buy lunch during a sales call, and provide tickets to a community activity.

prompt: A salesperson who sells 25 widgets to Internet Company A for one price and 25 widgets to Internet Company B for a higher price is involved in price
explanation: Discrimination. Price discrimination is an illegal activity in which a business charges different customers different prices for similar amounts and types of products. If a salesperson sells the same product in the same amounts to different customers and charges different prices, the salesperson is involved in price discrimination. Price competition is a type of rivalry between or among businesses that focuses on the use of price to attract scarce customer dollars. Charging different prices for the same product is not price segmentation or price misrepresentation.

prompt: The step of the selling process which tries to lead the customer to make a buying decision is
explanation: Reaching closure. All steps of the selling process are intended to lead toward making a sale, but that is the focus of reaching closure. In this phase, the salesperson tries to identify and resolve any remaining objections the customer may have and asks the customer to buy. Establishing relationships occurs at the beginning of the selling process and is followed by discovering client needs and prescribing solutions to those needs.
